heroText: Visby works best as a base in Sweden when you anchor days around Visby city wall, Stora Torget and Botanical Garden. Use those sights to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Visby International Airport handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

history.label: 12th century
history.text: In the 12th century, Visby Cathedral, dedicated to Saint Mary, was constructed.

history.label: 13th century
history.text: It was reshaped in the 13th century to its current appearance, and was officially opened in 1225, by the bishop of the Swedish city of Linköping (in regional map).

history.label: 14th century
history.text: In the Gutasagan (mid 14th century) the place is referred to as just Wi meaning "holy place, place of worship".
In 1361, Gotland was conquered by Valdemar IV of Denmark.
In 1391, 1394 and 1398, it was taken and plundered by the Victual Brothers, pirates who sailed the Baltic Sea.
An invading army of Teutonic Knights conquered Gotland in 1398, destroyed Visby and expelled the Victual Brothers.

history.label: 15th century
history.text: Around 1300, it was rebuilt to reach its current height, acquiring the characteristic towers, although some towers were not constructed until the 15th century.

In 1409, Grand Master Ulrich von Jungingen of the Teutonic Knights guaranteed peace with the Kalmar Union of Scandinavia by selling the island of Gotland to Queen Margaret of Denmark, Norway and Sweden.

In 1411, the Norwegian, Danish and Swedish King Eric of Pomerania had the castle of Visborg constructed, and settled himself there for 12 years, during which the city virtually became a pirates' nest, and.

history.label: Civic role
history.text: It was inhabited as early as the Stone Age, probably because of the access to fresh water and a natural harbour.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: 1,800 Gotlanders were killed in battle in front of the city.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: In the Danish throne quarrel, Lübeck, a Free City of the Holy Roman Empire and a leading member of the Hanseatic League, supported Frederick I, while Søren Norby the Danish governor of Gotland fought.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: While Norby fought a military action in Sweden, the Lübeckers successfully attacked Visby and set the city on fire from four sites.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Mary's Cathedral remained the last functional church and became the new city parish.
